The Master remains free, Minya remains missing, and Odin seeks vengeance for the city Cal unknowingly destroyed.

recaps.text: Previously: Cal is a sentient Dungeon Core beneath the Silverwood Tree, and Dani is the wisp bound to him as his partner and co-creator. Dale is an adventurer linked to Cal through a beast core and has become the baron responsible for the settlement surrounding the dungeon. Hans, Rose, Adam, and Tom form Dale's core adventuring party. Frank, Craig, Chandra, Amber, Brianna, Beor, Tyler, Henry, and Marie belong to the wider network of guild, political, commercial, and magical interests around Mountaindale. The dungeon's growth has made Dale's territory important to multiple peoples and kingdoms, while its dangers require him to protect both residents and adventurers.

Cal emerges from a period of impaired memory to find his dungeon damaged, its traps and creatures dangerously distorted, and Dani still missing. A memory gem confirms that his instability killed adventurers, while Minya warns that the council may destroy him if he threatens the continent. Cal begins repairing the dungeon, improving corruption control, automating defenses, and sending tracking insects to find Dani. He also redesigns rewards around floor-marked tokens instead of easy gold. Dale tells Hans, Rose, Adam, and Tom that Cal is sentient and that his own beast core links them. Cal pushes Dale to become strong enough to help recover Dani, and Dale learns to draw essence directly from beast cores through his gauntlet, though the first attempt costs him a finger. Tyler hires the party to collect dungeon specimens, while Craig trains Dale in earth techniques. Bob, Cal's goblin shaman, develops traps and infernal rituals as the dungeon's inhabitants become more capable. By the end of chapter 8, the token economy is changing how adventurers approach the dungeon, and both Cal and Dale are preparing for greater risks.

Cal automates creature production and treasure exchanges as he prepares to ascend, but his first production ritual causes a fatal surface collapse. Dale handles delegations seeking access to the dungeon and Silverwood Tree. Brianna supports his authority, the Amazons accept binding terms, and Beor uses his restored princely status to advance dwarf trade talks. Meanwhile, Dani's captors create an infernal dungeon through sacrifice and try to use her bond with Cal as leverage. She refuses to cooperate. Cal enters the Tower of Ascension, rejects lesser laws and a path associated with madness, and convinces the supreme law to accept both his ambition and imperfection. He emerges at B-rank, bound to Quintessence, but his condensed aura is deadly to his existing creatures until he expands the dungeon. Dale's party finds the dungeon strangely quiet while negotiations produce broad support for an international academy. Henry and Marie help develop access arrangements, and the dwarves offer construction. Dale reaches D-rank 6 after Craig teaches him to store excess essence in his aura, though his inefficient technique and the risk of corruption threaten his future advancement.

Cal reconnects to his dungeon, discovers a deep cavern of crude oil containing many essence types, and advances again while Minya supplies forbidden runes and preserved creature blood. He opens a fifth floor ruled by a poisonous flying manticore and extends long-distance communication through his bond with Minya. An infernal faction prepares an assault on Mountaindale and sends a team to seize Cal's core. Necromancers and undead overrun the town, forcing Dale, Richard, and other defenders to evacuate civilians into a refuge floor. Cal fights back through goblins, rituals, a controlled avatar, and the new manticore, while Dale's party continues rescuing townspeople. The High Inquisitor arrives and destroys several necrotic mages after judging them guilty, though Adam fears having his own past exposed. On the fifth floor, the manticore kills two attackers and poisons their leader before being fatally wounded. The final surviving necromancer betrays that leader, removes Cal's physical core from beneath the Silverwood Tree, and escapes through a portal with both the stolen core and the dying mage's body.

The invaders withdraw after taking hostages, and the High Inquisitor confronts his father, only to find that his own judgment registers the accused mass murderer as innocent. Cal recovers enough control to expand his influence over the town, establish a memory-funded crafting area, and build a large underground essence network with Bob. Dale confirms the attack's losses while the surviving factions agree to support the academy. He also forces Cal into a formal alliance that protects Mountaindale, regulates the dungeon's early floors, and ends Cal's covert influence over Dale's thoughts. A report of flying spiders places Dani in the Amazon capital, and Minya goes there to investigate. Cal prepares to move the entire dungeon while Dale opens Phantom Academy as a multi-race institution. After Minya reports a necromancer concentration in the capital's sewers and then falls silent, Cal captures a monostorm through his obelisks. He uses its power and a giant stabilizing mechanism to lift Mountaindale, the mountain, and its surrounding land into the air, beginning a rescue expedition despite the enormous continuing demand for essence.

The flying island must keep gathering essence to remain aloft. Cal activates a ley-line ritual in lightning territory, but the altered network catastrophically drains a nearby storm and destroys a city. Three lightning cultivators survive in crow-like bodies, and their leader abandons the name Jasper for Odin, vowing to find survivors and hunt the unknown destroyer. Cal does not yet recognize his responsibility. As Mountaindale approaches the Amazon capital, reports blame a figure called the Master for killing rulers and collapsing kingdoms. Chandra knows of him and believes he should be dead. The capital is already ruined and saturated with infernal essence, but Cal detects Dani there and commits to an attack. Marie swears lifelong service to Cal for the means to reclaim her kingdom. Cal remakes her as a dungeon-bound battlefield commander, and Henry accepts the same bond and receives his own enhanced equipment. Ordinary dungeon activity stops while Cal mobilizes a large goblin army. The coalition prepares to land the island, strike the necromantic occupation, and search the devastated city for Dani and any surviving residents.

Cal's coalition lands in the ruined capital and fights toward the infernal dungeon beneath it. Goblin totems extend Cal's influence across the battlefield while Rose, Tom, Chandra, Richard, Dale's party, and allied mages battle undead, demons, and necromancers. Richard banishes demons with their summoner, and Chandra kills an A-rank necromancer who confirms the Master's political aims. The Master is absent, but the coalition breaks into the central ritual chamber. Frank is mortally blighted before Brianna kills his attacker. The remaining necromancers seize Dani and escape through an unstable portal. Dale's attempt to stop them instead stabilizes the passage, catastrophically damages his core, and collapses his affinity channels, yet he follows. Across the portal, Dale destroys the infernal core intended to restore Dani, allowing her to escape, but the necromancers kill him. Cal discovers that the portal reaches through time and that Dale's death and transformed core are his own origin. After Dale's companions return, Cal absorbs the abandoned body, reunites with Dani, and reconstructs Dale as an independent person. Cal and Dani's renewed bond creates their daughter Grace. Dale resumes leadership but remains dependent on Cal's city for mana, while Cal turns his attention toward the still-free Master.

characters.description: A Coast Guard veteran in his late twenties who steps outside in boxer shorts and a pair of borrowed Crocs to retrieve his former girlfriend's runaway show cat, minutes before every building on Earth is collapsed by the alien Borant Corporation. Entering the dungeon underdressed and shoeless, he finds the game's System treats his condition as a running novelty and rewards it with unusual bonuses. Practical, stubborn, and slow to anger, he favors his fists and feet, explosives, and careful planning over flash, and from the first floor he refuses to perform cruelty for the watching audience or abandon weaker survivors, a stance that begins to define his reputation.
characters.name: Carl

aliases: Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk
characters.description: A pedigreed Persian show cat belonging to Carl's former girlfriend. An item from one of her first reward boxes raises her intelligence far beyond a normal animal's, and she soon speaks, casts spells, and, on the strength of her superior stats, insists on formal leadership of their two-member party, the self-styled Royal Court of Princess Donut. Vain, imperious, and devoted to her own comfort and status as a champion show animal, she treats Carl as staff as often as partner, yet the two quickly become inseparable and each repeatedly risks everything for the other.
characters.name: Princess Donut

characters.description: Carl's former girlfriend and Princess Donut's owner, away from home when the surface world was destroyed. She never enters the dungeon, but her absence leaves her prize cat in Carl's care and sets the whole story in motion.
characters.name: Beatrice

characters.description: The gruff non-player manager of a tutorial guild hall near the spot where Carl and Donut enter the first floor. After making Carl prove himself against the local goblins, he takes the pair in, walks them through the dungeon's rules, menus, loot, and dangers, and coaches them on how to build their characters. His advice is blunt and transactional at first, but he steadily becomes their most trusted source of guidance.
characters.name: Mordecai

characters.description: A caregiver from the Meadow Lark elder-care facility who entered the dungeon alongside a large group of elderly residents and fellow staff. Calm and quietly formidable, she leads the effort to keep dozens of vulnerable people alive, and her group's alliance with Carl and Donut carries both parties through a major boss fight on the first floor.
characters.name: Imani

characters.description: The alien host of a popular intergalactic interview program who brings notable crawlers onto her show between fights. Shrewd and theatrical, she takes an early interest in Carl and Donut, and her questions and off-air advice give the pair some of their first real insight into how the game and its audience actually work.
characters.name: Odette

characters.description: An elderly, sharp-tongued survivor traveling with the Meadow Lark group on the second floor. Carl helps her reach a safe room during a monster attack, and she repays the debt with loyalty, humor, and open flirtation. Despite her age she is a genuine fighter, and she becomes one of the pair's lasting allies.
characters.name: Elle McGibbons

characters.description: A public-relations liaison assigned to Carl and Donut by the game's operators once the pair start drawing serious audience attention. Zev manages their show bookings and sponsor contacts and explains how crawler appearances on Syndicate programs work, and despite working for the other side becomes genuinely fond of the team.
characters.name: Zev

characters.description: A prince of the Skull Empire, a porcine galactic monarchy whose citizens follow the crawl as entertainment. Carl and Donut first encounter him as a celebrity presence on a rival dungeon program, where he torments human crawlers for sport. Carl's willingness to defy him on the air plants the seed of a dangerous grudge between the crawlers and the Empire.
characters.name: The Maestro

characters.description: A juvenile pack-hunting dinosaur that Donut claims from a reward room near the end of the second floor and, after a fraught taming period involving several bites to her nose, adopts as her beloved pet and mount. Ferociously loyal to Donut, he rounds out the Royal Court as its animal muscle.
characters.name: Mongo

recaps.ending: The book ends with Carl and Princess Donut completing the second floor and descending the stairs to the third. Behind them, the second floor's great crisis is resolved: Carl destroyed the rampaging Rage Elemental with a vehicle rigged full of bombs and an exploit the whole universe watched, after the creature killed Yolanda and other members of the Meadow Lark group. The surviving Meadow Lark residents, shepherded by Imani and the Andrews brothers, went down ahead of them. On the way to the stairs Carl gambled his celebrity on a rival show to help the trapped crawlers Li Jun, Li Na, and Zhang escape, earning the enmity of the Maestro, a prince of the porcine Skull Empire, and Carl's on-air insolence toward the Empire is already infamous. Donut has tamed Mongo, a young dinosaur who joins the party as her pet. In an epilogue on Odette's talk show, the pair discuss the coming race and class selection that will reshape every crawler on the third floor, and Odette leaves Donut with a private piece of advice about choosing a class. The crawler population has fallen below a million, the game's operators are both profiting from and unsettled by the pair's popularity, and Carl goes down the stairs resolved not just to survive the dungeon but to beat the people who built it.
recaps.in_short: The alien Borant Corporation collapses every building on Earth, kills most of humanity, and turns the planet into an eighteen-floor dungeon broadcast across the galaxy as entertainment. Carl, caught outside in his boxer shorts chasing his ex-girlfriend's show cat, enters the dungeon with the cat, Princess Donut, who gains human intelligence from an early reward and becomes a talking spellcaster who insists on leading their party. Guided by Mordecai, a gruff tutorial-guild manager, they fight through the first floor's goblins and bosses, ally with the elderly survivors of the Meadow Lark care facility, and become breakout stars of the broadcast. On the second floor Carl kills a devastating Rage Elemental with a bomb-rigged vehicle in front of the whole universe, the pair appear on Odette's intergalactic talk show, Carl makes an enemy of the Skull Empire's Prince Maestro while rescuing trapped crawlers on a rival program, and Donut tames a pet dinosaur, Mongo. The book closes with the trio descending to the third floor, where every surviving crawler must choose a new race and class.

recaps.text: The alien Borant Corporation instantly collapses every building on Earth, killing everyone inside, and announces that survivors may reclaim their planet by conquering an eighteen-floor World Dungeon whose entrances stay open only briefly. Carl, outside in boxer shorts and his ex-girlfriend's Crocs to retrieve her show cat Princess Donut, has no other way to survive the cold and enters the dungeon with the cat. On the first floor he kills a goblin to earn shelter in a tutorial guild run by Mordecai, who becomes their guide, and completes the tutorial, learning that roughly thirteen million humans have entered and that the crawl is a galactic broadcast run for an audience. A reward from an early loot box transforms Donut: she gains human-level intelligence and speech, and with stats higher than Carl's she formally becomes party leader of the self-declared Royal Court of Princess Donut. Carl, still without shoes or pants, starts to accumulate the fighting skills, oddball achievements, and explosive habits that will define him.

Carl and Donut settle into the rhythm of the first floor: grinding low-level monsters, sheltering in safe rooms staffed by non-player attendants, and learning the dungeon's economy of loot boxes, achievements, and fan attention. They defeat their first boss, an encounter that leaves Carl shaken by how the game dresses its victims. The first broadcast recap episode airs, showing the pair glimpses of other notable crawlers, including the unsettling child prodigy Lucia Mar. They find evidence of crawlers murdering crawlers, tied to a man named Frank Q. Donut discovers the chat system, and her charisma, together with Carl's goblin-friendly tattoo, lets the pair strike a bargain with two goblin engineers, trading salvage for a ramshackle vehicle instead of fighting.

The goblin alliance ends in fire: Carl loots the goblin workshop and destroys it, an act the System memorializes with achievements he is not proud of. The pair earn passes to the Desperado Club, an underground establishment for crawlers, and survive their first direct brush with the player-killers Frank Q and Maggie My, escaping an attempted ambush in a safe room. Riding their goblin-built vehicle east for hours, they follow spray-painted signs left by other survivors and find the people who made them: a band from the Meadow Lark elder-care facility, led by the caregiver Imani with the Andrews brothers and dozens of elderly residents in tow. The two groups exchange stories and begin planning to reach the floor's exit together.

Allied with the Meadow Lark group, Carl and Donut grind the surrounding tunnels, conceal the group's trail, and take down the Juicer, a boss guarding the neighborhood. After a stop at a training guild to learn new spells and finally armor Carl's hands, the combined force fights the area's true gatekeeper, a massive boss called the Ball of Swine, and defeats it using a fortified redoubt. Now level ten, Carl and Donut agree to keep helping Meadow Lark's residents reach safety. As the pair descend toward the second floor they are teleported out of the dungeon to a production trailer: their growing fame has earned them a booking on Dungeon Crawler After Hours, the intergalactic talk show hosted by Odette.

On Odette's show Donut charms the galaxy while Carl studies how the game is packaged for its audience; afterward Odette talks candidly with them about the crawl, the coming race selection, and the fact that random loot is not truly random. On the second floor the pair fight new monsters, and Carl helps the elderly Elle McGibbons to safety as the broadcast warns that Rage Elementals will be released on the floor. Carl weaponizes his growing crafting skill, building his first signature bombs. When the pair try to skip a boss chamber, the boss, a clone of a monster called the Krakaren, comes to them: Carl kills it with a massive explosion and nearly dies shielding Donut with his own body, and Donut, dragging him to safety, admits how much he means to her.

Recovering, the pair find Mordecai transformed into a new body, meet their first Borant dungeon administrator, and gain a public-relations liaison, Zev, who manages their growing celebrity. They rejoin the Meadow Lark group for the push to the stairs, but disaster strikes: a resident's harmless accident triggers the release of a Rage Elemental as punishment, and the creature kills Yolanda and another member of the group before the survivors reach shelter. With the game's rules newly changed to stop crawlers from waiting out the floor in safe rooms, Carl builds a bomb-rigged vehicle and, with the entire universe watching, leads the Rage Elemental on a wild chase and destroys it through a chain of bombs, obstacles, and a rules exploit that becomes an instant broadcast legend.

The Meadow Lark survivors descend to the third floor ahead of them while Carl and Donut finish the second. Pulled onto the sadistic rival show Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, Carl gambles on his own ratings value to help the trapped crawlers Li Jun, Zhang, and Li Jun's sister Li Na escape an impossible fight, defying the Maestro, a prince of the porcine Skull Empire, whose grudge against Carl becomes public news. The broadcast reports the crawler population falling below one million. Clearing the local kobold territory, the pair defeat the boss guarding the stairwell, and in its reward room Donut claims Mongo, a juvenile dinosaur she tames, after several bites, into her devoted pet. With Mongo in tow, Carl and Donut take the stairs down to the third floor, where every crawler must soon choose a new race and class.

characters.description: A sentient Dungeon Core who is expanding his domain while carrying a community aboard a flying mountain. He lives with Dani and their infant wisp, experiments freely with dungeon creatures and devices, and follows ley lines toward an obstruction that is limiting the flow of essence.
characters.name: Cal

characters.description: Cal's wisp, partner, and fellow dungeon manager. She cares for Grace and challenges Cal when his experiments endanger visitors or distract him from essential work, giving the young wisp firmer guidance than Cal's permissive approach provides.
characters.name: Dani

characters.description: The tiny, nonverbal wisp child of Cal and Dani. Her curiosity and playfulness are already dangerous within a lethal dungeon, as shown when she draws cats toward adventuring parties without understanding the consequences.
characters.name: Grace

characters.description: Cal's goblin shaman and the leading worker among the many goblins called Bob. He directs inscription projects and keeps the dungeon's ley-line map current, making him a central organizer for Cal's technical plans.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: A cultivator rebuilding meridians damaged by extreme exertion and a recent death. He and Cal are divided forms of one original person, and their reunited souls left each with some of the other's fading memories. Dale trains while helping Cal pursue blocked ley lines.
characters.name: Dale

characters.description: Dale's exacting combat and cultivation teacher. He uses painful, survival-focused exercises to make Dale control essence without gestures, beginning with the precise movement of enclosing stone rather than its destruction.
characters.name: Moon-elf instructor

characters.description: The leader behind an expanding undead and demonic campaign. His forces offer besieged communities submission, then kill and reanimate those who resist, making his advance the central military threat facing the allied peoples.
characters.name: Master

characters.description: A powerful council member who questions whether the flying mountain should devote its people and resources to Cal's ley-line objective. She presses the council to distinguish known dangers from assumptions while it debates war, peace, and covert action.
characters.name: Chandra

characters.description: Dale's dark-elf political ally and a strategic voice on the council. Rather than attack the enemy leader directly at an impossible price, she proposes weakening the campaign through targeted strikes against its generals.
characters.name: Brianna

characters.description: An allied king serving on the flying mountain's council. Faced with reports of conquered cities and possible mass sacrifice, he argues for immediate war while Dale urges the council to consider whether negotiation might preserve more lives.
characters.name: Henry

characters.description: A C-rank philosopher and administrator selected to lead the academy on a three-month probation. He developed his own cultivation technique relatively late in life, and the council considers that achievement alongside his unconventional background.
characters.name: Academy headmaster

characters.description: The senior member and practical combat mentor in Dale's raid party. During the descent into an underwater dungeon, he interprets Dale's unusually pure essence as the reason for slow aura growth and the basis for greater strength after advancement.
characters.name: Hans

characters.description: A bow user with chaotic essence who joins Dale's five-person raid into an underwater dungeon. She is an experienced, decisive fighter, killing an attacking octopus as the party crosses the dungeon's flooded environment.
characters.name: Rose

characters.description: A northern barbarian and powerful close-range fighter in Dale's dungeon party. He brings direct physical force to a group entering an unscouted aquatic environment where predators and dense water essence create unfamiliar dangers.
characters.name: Tom

characters.description: A celestial cultivator and healer in Dale's party, recently advanced to D-rank 6. He removes the underwater dungeon's blue core, forcing the group into a desperate escape as water rises through the now-unregulated structure.
characters.name: Adam

characters.description: Cal's B-rank man-eating manticore and a dungeon floor boss built for traps and ambushes. Five B-rank mages lose two companions before defeating him, but Cal can restore Manny after a successful challenge.
characters.name: Manny

characters.description: Dale's monk instructor for aura work and an associate of Hans. He replaces hazardous whole-body experimentation with disciplined practice in the palms, teaching exact affinity ratios and practical shields before specialized combinations.
characters.name: Craig

characters.description: A dungeon affiliate who recruits prospective servants for Cal. She asks him to shelter them in his protected mage settlement and accepts that entry will require binding oaths, placing her between Cal's needs and the people she has organized.
characters.name: Minya

characters.description: The goblin who pilots the flying mountain through its first landing. Cal credits him with bringing it down successfully.
characters.name: Navigation Bob

characters.description: A lethal dungeon enforcer present when Minya's recruits swear service to Cal. Snowball kills a recruit who tries to flee the binding oath, helping impose Cal's strict authority over the new attendants.
characters.name: Snowball

characters.description: A Guild enforcer whose soul-infused attack converts targets into essence or mana. He erases Cal's control over an entire dungeon floor and threatens the whole settlement, forcing the flying dungeon into Guild military service.
characters.name: Guild S-rank commander

characters.description: A newly ascended heavenly-rank ritual-maker who destroys the colossal undead construct and seizes control of the battlefield's remains. He presents universal destruction as a solution to suffering while raising the dead into an immense ritual.
characters.name: High Inquisitor's father

characters.description: A senior necromancer who halts a destructive subordinate during a dispute over battlefield remains. He demands coexistence between former enemies, agrees to meet Dale's council, and recognizes that Dale and Cal share one soul.
characters.name: Necromancer leader

characters.description: A volatile mage who attempts to gas a crowd during a dispute over battlefield remains. The necromancer leader interrupts the attack and forces the opposing groups to stand down.
characters.name: Destructive mage

characters.description: A High Magus and rune specialist directing the coalition's technical assessment. She judges that relocating the moon-binding runes may be possible, but only with weeks of work, extensive materials, and large-scale rune production.
characters.name: Amber

characters.description: An overwhelmingly powerful being Dale encounters during ascension. It claims a bond to his soul, shows him a projected future of mana collapse followed by restoration, and says survival depends on Cal and an undisclosed hard choice.
characters.name: Cosmic entity

recaps.ending: The coalition fails to finish its portal-based rune relocation before the smaller moon reaches the world. Dale takes the last viable course, sitting within the binding script while the necromancer leader and allied mages activate Cal's untested support runes. Dale manifests disenchanting water, nullifies the magic touching him, and breaks the script. Its released force is driven upward, and the moon implodes into fragments rather than striking the world. Dale enters the Tower of Ascension and returns physically remade with an unnamed attainment. A cosmic entity has shown him that falling debris and prolonged winter will be compounded by Cal's ley lines draining loose mana and essence, killing mana-dependent peoples while humanity survives in a diminished age. The same projected future requires Cal's eventual transformation to restore mana, lost peoples, and prosperity. Cal is newly A-rank and still controls the flying dungeon and spreading ley lines. Dani and Grace survive. Adam is dead, Hans and Rose are married, Tom still faces his uncontrolled rage, and the High Inquisitor's father remains unresolved. Dale now intends to save the world from Cal's coming desolation while preserving Cal's necessary future role.
recaps.in_short: Cal carries a settlement aboard his flying dungeon while extending ley lines across the world, and Dale rebuilds his damaged cultivation under increasingly harsh instruction. Guild coercion draws them into war against the Master's undead forces. Adam dies saving the army, but the battle is superseded when the High Inquisitor's father sacrifices leading combatants to pull the smaller moon toward the world. Former enemies unite around Cal's runes, yet their relocation plan cannot finish in time. Dale uses disenchanting water to break the binding script while Cal's auxiliary runes direct its power upward, imploding the moon and averting impact. During ascension, Dale sees that the debris, winter, and Cal's essence-draining ley lines will cause mass extinction. He also learns that Cal's later transformation is necessary to restore the world. Dale returns remade and committed to stopping the coming desolation without losing the future Cal must eventually create.

recaps.text: Previously: Cal is a sentient Dungeon Core whose expanding home supports a settlement and academy aboard a flying mountain. Dani is his wisp and partner, and Dale previously recovered her after she was taken from the dungeon. Dale is an adventurer and cultivator whose circle includes Hans, Tom, Adam, and Rose. Cal and Dale remain closely connected despite their very different forms and responsibilities, while the people around them depend on the dungeon for safety, training, and power.

Cal experiments with dungeon creatures, recording devices, and training floors while guiding the flying mountain toward an obstruction in a major ley-line junction. Dale, still repairing burned-out meridians after his death, learns non-somatic essence control from a severe moon-elf instructor. Cal equips him with valuable affinity-resistant clothing, though it remains vulnerable to crushing force. The council debates whether to fight the Master, seek peace, or assassinate his generals. Dale then leads Hans, Rose, Tom, and Adam into an underwater dungeon. Adam removes its core, and the party escapes through rapidly rising water. Cal destroys the nonsentient captured core and redirects the abandoned dungeon's excess power through his ley-line network, removing the blockage. The flying mountain resumes its journey with improved access to surface essence. Meanwhile, five B-rank mages defeat Manny, Cal's manticore boss, at significant cost.

Dale studies aura interactions with Craig and develops the beginnings of regenerative and specialized shields, while Cal finishes a restricted refuge for mages and relocates his core there. Minya brings recruits who seek the dungeon's protection, and Cal accepts them only under binding service oaths. His growing ley-line system delivers tainted essence faster than he can safely use it, while a high-rank plant mage broadens her plant law into a stronger nature law. When Minya's recruits arrive, Snowball kills one who tries to flee rather than swear, and Cal kills another who refuses the required work. A recovered Guild return bell suggests that the organization has planted an informant. The political danger then becomes direct: a Guild liaison announces that Dale's supporting kingdoms have fallen and strips him of his human titles, property authority, and control over the dungeon and academy. Brianna maintains that Dale's dark-elf authority survives, but publicly he has been reduced to an ordinary D-rank cultivator under Guild wartime rule.

Dale gains limited protection by becoming the academy headmaster's direct disciple, although the arrangement is transactional and his advancement quotas remain. The Guild's S-rank commander then destroys an entire dungeon floor and threatens to consume Cal's core unless the flying mountain serves the war. Cal outwardly complies while searching for a defense. Dale's party commits to sustained dungeon training, and Cal creates protected rest areas that cannot be exploited for cultivation. Minya leads a separate group to seize a mage-ranked dungeon core needed for the next ley-line blockage. Dale learns to absorb monster cores efficiently through the rune in his palm, reaches D-rank 5, and continues building an unusually dense external aura instead of rushing normal advancement. His group defeats Snowball without Hans's direct help, proving its improved coordination but exposing resentment over Hans's constant criticism. Dale's moon-elf instructor closes this phase by forcing him to detect concealed creatures through aura feedback, giving Dale a practical counter to visual camouflage.

After the flying mountain lands, Dale nearly harms himself cultivating with Cal's concentrated essence, then replaces his damaged cultivation structure with a stronger technique. Minya returns from an erupting volcano with a frightened dungeon core and its bonded wisp. Cal gives the rescued core authority over his early floors and uses the ruined volcano's escaping power to extend his ley lines. The Guild orders the flying mountain into the coming war. Dale, pressured by academy demands and conscription, clears a goblin fortification alone and becomes increasingly ruthless. He reaches D-rank 9, defeats a challenger, and threatens the clerk who withheld his contributions. Craig identifies the imbalance behind Dale's behavior and forces him to sacrifice rank in exchange for permanent bodily development, leaving him stronger but back at D-rank 1. As the mountain approaches the necromantic army, Cal prepares escape routes, armed goblins, and a trap for the S-rank commander. The settlement finally sees the enormous undead host, and the mountain waits behind enemy lines for the allied assault.

Dale rebuilds rapidly after Craig's intervention, completes the reinforcement of his body, and reaches C-rank as the flying mountain enters the war. His party joins the ground forces while much stronger combatants trade attacks that reshape the battlefield. Cal resolves his stalled cultivation by choosing an inner world capable of representing many laws as his future foundation. In battle, Dale develops a starlight aura that both heals allies and destroys undead. Rose, Hans, and Dale banish demons, but the enemy combines battlefield remains into a colossal undead construct that Dale's sector cannot withstand. Cal then activates his revised ley-line script. The world-spanning network gives him new perception along its routes and allows him to reverse the flow, making him both the source and recipient of a vast stream of power. Several sections remain blocked, and the activation leaves Cal exhausted even as it opens a path toward rapid advancement.

Power from Cal's ley lines floods his reservoir faster than he can safely contain it. The Silverwood Tree absorbs much of the excess while Cal experiments with the inner world that will support his cultivation. He refuses to risk Dani and Grace against the colossal undead construct and secretly alters the flying mountain's portal to preserve an escape option. On the battlefield, Dale's headmaster teaches him a celestial-light attack as demons overwhelm the party's position. Hans saves Rose, Tom collapses after banishing a demon, and Adam suffers a fatal wound. Adam's body releases a hardened celestial barrier that deflects the construct before he dissolves into golden light. Dale then kills the necromancer directing the local undead, causing many nearby enemies to collapse or withdraw. The High Inquisitor's father destroys the colossal construct, declares that he has reached heavenly rank, and raises the battlefield dead into a vast ritual intended to end all life. Former enemies unite against him but cannot stop him.

Cal identifies the new ritual as an attempt to pull the smaller moon into the world. Manny volunteers for a solo attack, coating part of the ritual in corrosive blood, and Cal drops the flying mountain onto the weakened point. The strike creates only a crack before the High Inquisitor's father throws the mountain aside, destroying much of it while Dani and Grace survive. The survivors learn that leading S-rank fighters from several peoples were sacrificed to power the ritual. The Master calls for a ceasefire and claims the father planted madness in him during childhood. Cal distrustfully returns to rescue stranded survivors after the Master asks for help. Grief drives Rose to attack Dale until Hans calms her. A necromancer leader then stops renewed conflict, agrees to meet Dale's council, and confirms that Dale and Cal share one soul. Amber and the council conclude that destroying the moon-binding runes would release catastrophic power. Their best remaining proposal is to relocate the runes so the moon is pulled away, a project requiring Cal's manufacturing abilities and more time than they may possess.

Cal builds a gravity-compressed elemental floor and continues extending ley lines that reduce dangerous local concentrations of mana. Tom settles his grievance against the necromancer leader through a single ceremonial blow, and Dale publicly explains how a chaos-damaged portal divided his original existence into Dale and Cal. Cal joins the anti-rune effort in exchange for forbidden knowledge and learns that A-rank requires a stable inner foundation able to store matter. He shapes that foundation, stores a rock, and reaches A-rank. The silverwood tree flowers, producing pollen sufficient for roughly a thousand elf births, while the moon-elf instructor claims the elemental floor as resistance training. The necromancer leader supplies Cal with secret runes and materials but admits he has little life remaining. Hans and Rose marry shortly before the operation, while Tom says he must master his berserker rage before returning to his family. The rune-maker leaves the site, the binding grows stronger, and the coalition concedes that its mobile portal will be completed too late. Dale proposes a final, highly dangerous alternative.

Cal cannot disable the moon-binding runes without abandoning his dungeon, so Dale executes his last plan. The necromancer leader and allied mages place Cal's untested runes around the script while Dale enters a trance at its center. Dale manifests disenchanting water that turns magic mundane, breaks the binding script, and survives the released power by nullifying what reaches him. Cal's auxiliary runes direct the discharge upward, imploding the smaller moon and preventing impact. Dale collapses and enters the Tower of Ascension. There he meets a cosmic entity that shows him the cost of victory: moon fragments and prolonged winter will combine with Cal's ley lines draining loose essence, causing the extinction of mana-dependent peoples and leaving humanity in a technological dark age. A later transformation by Cal restores essence, mana, and the lost peoples, producing the best projected future, but Dale must make an undisclosed hard choice. He returns physically remade with an unnamed attainment and declares that their next task is saving the world from the catastrophe Cal is destined to cause.

characters.description: The only male student in Halen's first-year class and leader of a party that has just reached level 4. His class, Emperor, could not be read by CIDs at the entrance exam, and he hides a secondary class, Demon Lord, drawn from a demon sealed inside him whose name, Snoo, he keeps to himself. His skills are Dark Strike, Earth Stomp, Charm, Metamorphosis, Sprint and Absorb. He has already killed classmates to keep his party safe and is ready to do so again. He is dating Dez and engaged to the elf Fayeth after an accidental proposal.
characters.name: Ken Nagato

characters.description: An elf who serves as the tank of Ken's party and is the daughter of the elven ambassador. Ken proposed to her without meaning to, and she now calls him her fieore, while he refers to her as his elven fiance. She shares Ken's bed along with Dez, who would like Fayeth to become physically closer to him. The anti-elf faction at Halen has tried to kill her before, though months have passed without a new attempt.
characters.name: Fayeth

characters.description: A warlock in Ken's party and his girlfriend, whose mother is a succubus. Dez provided the family ritual that sealed a demon inside Ken, and she inspects the seal regularly to confirm it is holding. She openly wants Fayeth to grow physically closer to Ken as well.
characters.name: Dez

characters.description: A druid who serves as the healer of Ken's party and is accompanied by her pet rabbit Bun Bun.
characters.name: Charlotte

characters.description: The bard of Ken's party. She is drawn to healers. She unknowingly played a part in Ken's victory over the demon sealed within him, something Ken has chosen not to tell her.
characters.name: Harley

characters.description: Charlotte's pet rabbit and constant companion. During the class camping drill he keeps watch alongside her, giving the party an extra lookout while the others set traps and alarm wires around the camp.
characters.name: Bun Bun

characters.description: The Aberrant-class instructor in charge of Ken's first-year class and his main patron. She moves the fifth-floor boss fight up to serve as the first-term final and sets up a flag contest across the first ten floors, in which any party that falls to zero points is expelled. In private she tells Ken the headmistress will not permit a purge, so the contest is the approved way to remove anti-elf students. She earlier supplied the blood of a powerful floor boss that helped Ken overcome his demon, and she intimidates students freely, wrecking one desk as a warning.
characters.name: Crimson

characters.description: Fayeth's father and the elven ambassador at Halen. He lives in the academy's visitor center alongside Crimson and Ken, and he is researching the first holder of the Emperor class, a class the elves link to periods of upheaval.
characters.name: Adin

characters.description: The headmistress of Halen. She has come to tolerate Ken because he improved the academy's relations with the elves, and she has granted him a small locker room as the school's male student. She does not want students purged outright, which leads Crimson to use a contest instead.
characters.name: Marlow

characters.description: A first-year who leads one of the other parties in Crimson's class. When Crimson announces the flag contest, Kendra's objection prompts the instructor to give every party a single starting point.
characters.name: Kendra

characters.description: A first-year in Crimson's class. Early in the term Crimson destroys Taylor's desk as a warning, an example of how the instructor deals with students in her room.
characters.name: Taylor

characters.description: A frost knight on Halen's security council, several levels above Ken, with the ability to slow her targets. During the gym camp-out she is near a marsh camp that Ken raids for its flag, and he manages to slip away from her.
characters.name: Penelope

characters.description: The demon lord sealed inside Ken and the source of his secondary Demon Lord class. Ken beat it in a stealth contest with the help of a high-level boss's blood supplied by Crimson, and he keeps its name a secret from everyone.
characters.name: Snoo

characters.description: A priestess in Halen's Class B who is hostile to the elves. Ken's party has learned that her father runs the company that makes CIDs, and that plant-grown elven CIDs could undercut his business, giving her family a motive to move against Fayeth and the elves.
characters.name: The Class B priestess

characters.description: Father of the anti-elf Class B priestess and head of the company that manufactures CIDs. Elven CIDs grown from plants threaten his firm's market, which Ken's party sees as the reason behind his family's hostility to the elves.
characters.name: The CID company head

characters.description: A first-year who leads the only other party in Crimson's class to have reached level 4 at the start of the term.
characters.name: The spell-weaver rival

characters.description: A Beastmaster in the spell-weaver rival's party who scouts with two wolves and an owl. Through her animals she saw a wealthy Class B student start the gym fire during the camp-out, and her leader passes this on to Ken when their parties meet in the dungeon.
characters.name: The rival party's scout

characters.description: A party of three men and a woman who climb up from the safe-zone pit into the fifth-floor boss room just as Ken arrives first at the end of his race with the rival party. Their sudden arrival alarms him.
characters.name: The four hunters

characters.description: The head of the United Guilds, a heavily scarred and muscular man staying at the Halen branch. He shows Ken records identifying the dungeon attackers as members of a low-level guild, most of them with prison histories. Because his organization must look neutral, he will not act against them openly, but he keeps the guild under watch, has already stopped two earlier attempts to send stronger killers, and discourages others by letting them know Crimson has been informed.
characters.name: The United Guilds president

characters.description: A dungeon advisor for the United Guilds at Halen. She watches Ken with obvious curiosity as he comes out of the guild president's office.
characters.name: Katie

characters.description: The sole grandfather among the five grandparents who raised Ken. When Ken phones home to ask for help against the guild targeting his party, the grandparents tease him about having three girlfriends. Once Fayeth introduces herself, they cancel their plans to fly and decide to make the trip on foot, expecting to arrive around midnight the following night.
characters.name: Ken's grandfather

characters.description: The stern member of the grandparents who raised Ken, and the only one related to him by blood. She looks like Ken's mother, her daughter, and blames herself for having been too harsh with her. In a private talk she promises to support Ken if he tells her everything, warning that any attack on the Nagato family will end in bloodshed. Ken tells her this is the third attempt on Fayeth.
characters.name: Ken's biological grandmother

characters.description: A close friend from Ken's mother's adventuring party whom Ken thought of as an uncle. According to Ken's grandfather, this friend wanted Ken's mother, grew jealous, and hired old enemies of the family to get rid of Ken's father. None of this has been confirmed.
characters.name: Ken's honorary uncle

characters.description: The heir to the elven throne, who is reported to hold an Emperor class, one of only two known. Ken finds the timing suspiciously convenient, given his own class, while Adin works to keep Ken's class out of view.
characters.name: The elven heir

characters.description: An elven royal censor, the trusted advisor of a noble lady who sent her to question Adin about documents on Ken's class. Royal censors serve the emperor's line as investigators, judges and executioners, and Adin fears them. Crimson escorts her and slices through her sword when she half draws it, warning that Ken's grandparents forbid weapons or harm to his relatives. The censor, who is wary of Crimson, says she will return in two days, and Crimson follows her into the dungeon.
characters.name: The royal censor

characters.description: One of Ken's four grandmothers, distinct from the other three. She meets the party in the first safe zone, buys beer, teases Ken, and lets a brief wave of killing intent show before announcing that the party will be leaving with her.
characters.name: Ken's safe-zone grandmother

characters.description: One of Ken's four grandmothers, who fights with banners and debuffs. At the close of the term she drives the party to the airport, where they are each given two parachutes for the strike against the CID company head.
characters.name: Ken's banner grandmother

characters.description: One of Ken's four grandmothers, a pilot with the power to revive the fallen. When the CID company head kills Ken with a shield blast during the fight after the plane crash, she brings Ken back to life.
characters.name: Ken's reviver grandmother

characters.description: A high-level portal caster with a snake tattoo running down both arms, matching the arch-and-snake mark worn by the CID company head's guards. He claims the title of heir, and Ken's grandfather despises the organization the mark represents. He summons reinforcements during the fight and escapes once the company head is killed.
characters.name: The snake-tattoo leader

recaps.ending: The term closes with Ken's party passing the semester by defeating the fifth-floor boggart boss. The anti-elf threat at Halen is finished: Fayeth killed the Class B priestess after her father's plane was downed, and Crimson turned her father, the CID company head, to dust. Ken was killed in that fight and revived by a grandmother. The convict guild is gone. Ken is level 5 with Dark Blades and Discharge and has accepted his place as heir to the family's assassin trade. He is soul-bonded to Fayeth and committed to Dez and Charlotte; Harley and Bun Bun remain in the party. The grandparents stay near Halen and plan to train the party. Open threads carry forward: the snake-tattoo leader and his organization escaped and are now linked to the CID company head; the fate of Ken's parents and the friend accused of betraying his father remain unconfirmed; Crimson's heart-rate-linked ability is still dangerous, and she believes Ken is her best chance at fixing it while aiming to push him to floor 20; the elves' staged Emperor claim and the request that Ken share Absorb with the princess remain unresolved, with Ken committed only to visiting the elven world; the Naga threat deep in the dungeon persists; the seal holding Snoo has shifted; and Charlotte's sisters have yet to test Ken. Ken and Fayeth look ahead to four years of hard leveling.
recaps.in_short: In his first year at Halen, Ken Nagato leads his level-4 party through Crimson's flag contest, a sanctioned way to expel the anti-elf students who target his elven fiance Fayeth. A fire set during the gym camp-out leaves him with strained mana channels, and Crimson trains him hard in weighted mana-suppression cuffs. On a race to the fifth-floor boss, hired hunters from a convict guild ambush the party; Ken lures them off alone and kills them with his friends' help. His grandparents arrive, revealing that the family are hereditary assassins, and Ken wipes out the guild's house in a single night, then asks them to rebuild the family trade. He bonds fully with Fayeth, steals the Class B priestess's flag, reaches level 5, and learns from an elven royal censor that the princess's Emperor class was staged, leaving his own as the true one. After the party defeats the priestess underground and beats the fifth-floor boss, her father threatens Halen. Ken's grandfather crashes his plane, and in the fight that follows Ken is killed and revived, Crimson destroys the father, Fayeth kills the priestess, and a snake-tattooed portal caster whose mark matches the CID company head's guards escapes.

recaps.text: Previously: Ken Nagato enrolled at Halen as its only male first-year and landed in the Aberrant class under the formidable instructor Crimson. His class, Emperor, could not be read by the CIDs that track adventurers. A ritual provided by his girlfriend Dez, a warlock whose mother is a succubus, sealed a demon lord named Snoo inside him and gave him the secondary class Demon Lord. With blood from a high-level floor boss supplied by Crimson, and an assist from Harley that she never learned about, Ken won a contest against the demon, though he keeps its name to himself. His party came together around him: the druid healer Charlotte with her rabbit Bun Bun, the bard Harley, Dez, and the elf tank Fayeth, daughter of the elven ambassador, to whom Ken proposed by accident and who now holds him to it. An anti-elf faction among the students made attempts on Fayeth's life, and Ken killed students to protect his party; on the opening day of term, Crimson herself put to death two students who went after Harley. Ken's role in improving relations with the elves earned him grudging tolerance from Headmistress Marlow. As this book opens, the party has reached level 4, and they have learned that a Class B priestess at the heart of the anti-elf hostility is the daughter of the man whose company makes CIDs, a business that elven CIDs grown from plants could threaten.

So far this book: Months after the last attempt on Fayeth, Ken's party is level 4 and training daily. Crimson makes the fifth-floor boss the first-term final and launches a flag contest over the first ten floors, where parties gain or lose points through stolen flags and photos of camps, and a party at zero is expelled. She tells Ken privately that this is the approved route to removing anti-elf students. The party wins a classroom camping drill, with Ken stealing flags and using Absorb publicly for the first time. That night the whole first-year class camps in the gym. Ken's party shares a fortified forest camp with Kendra's group under a truce, and the anti-elf priestess, who has filled the places of three party members Ken killed, asks him on a date before Dez cuts her off. Fayeth urges Ken to pursue Charlotte, who feels overshadowed; while Ken plays decoy so that Charlotte and Bun Bun can steal flags, he and Charlotte kiss and she admits she likes him. Ken evades Penelope of the security council during a marsh raid. Attackers probe the camp, and then a large fire is set in the gym. Dez calls Ken back, and he absorbs the flames again and again to clear an exit, straining his mana channels until he collapses. Crimson, who could not intervene without ending the exercise, bows to him in apology, and Ken suspects the anti-elf faction. The party learns it was disqualified for storing captured flags in their CIDs, and Dez finds that Ken's seal has shifted. Crimson takes Ken into the mountains for harsh training, locking on mana-suppression cuffs that grow heavier as he strains and offering him extra days of her service for points scored in sparring.

So far this book: Ken spars with Crimson for a full day and night, absorbing mana she pours into him, and finally lands a hit she tells him to keep quiet. The session, powered by potions worth more than a house, raises his stats by seven points without a level gain. The party then sets out on a multi-day dive aimed at the fifth-floor boss, a giant boggart carrying fribbits, about half a year early, with camping gear from Crimson. On the fourth floor fribbits fuse into boggarts, and Fayeth starts launching Ken off her shield to strike their high cores. In camp, Ken and Dez affirm their love, and Fayeth tells Charlotte the three of them will be family. The spell-weaver rival's party arrives; its scout reportedly saw a wealthy Class B student start the gym fire, and the two parties agree to race to the boss room without fighting the boss. Ken wins the sprint, but four strangers rise from the safe-zone pit with obvious intent to kill. Ken has both parties hit the boss so its door begins to close, trapping the strangers inside while everyone flees. Suspecting the hunters track CIDs, Ken sends his party toward the surface, takes all their CIDs, and draws the hunters off alone, carrying a weakness scroll from the rival leader's father. His poisoned ambush and a Charm that turns the leader against their healer only go so far, and the axe-wielding woman corners him. His party and the rival group, who followed without their CIDs, arrive in time; Ken kills the woman and the rest are cut down. Dez slaps him for his solo plan, which he admits was partly a test of the rivals, and then forgives him.

So far this book: On the surface, the United Guilds president shows Ken that the hunters came from a low-level guild of former convicts; the organization must look neutral but will keep watch. The party spends its earnings: Harley buys the dress she had saved for, Ken spends 43,000 coins on Dark Blades, which adds magic to his weapon strikes, Charlotte learns Cleanse for the scorpion floors, and Dez learns Demon's Eye. Ken reports to Crimson, claims the convict guild as his own target, and phones the grandparents who raised him. After Fayeth introduces herself as his fieore, they set off for Halen on foot, and his biological grandmother privately warns that attacking the Nagato family brings bloodshed. In class Crimson teaches boss-room procedure, then gives Ken leave to act in the city as long as no Halen students die. Ken takes Dez, Charlotte and Fayeth out for sushi; the four agree to stay united, and Ken promises to wait until Charlotte is ready for intimacy. Adin tries the leftover sushi and holds private talks with Crimson. Despite Ken's barricades, the grandparents slip a knife-pinned note into his room overnight, and Ken admits to Dez that his upbringing trained him to kill. He tells Fayeth that protecting his partners is his purpose. At the visitor center the grandfather ambushes him, and the grandmothers set up a tea room where Crimson serves them with rare deference. Ken lays out the anti-elf faction and the industrial family's daughter leading its attacks. Crimson notes that an upcoming event offers a way to expel her, and the biological grandmother declares the convict guild will be wiped out, with Ken delivering the blow.

So far this book: Ken's grandfather tells him that his father was removed through the scheming of a jealous close friend from his mother's party, someone Ken regarded as an uncle, who hired the family's old enemies; nothing is confirmed. The grandfather provokes Crimson with a rival magazine, uncovers Ken's Demon Lord secondary class, and discusses the Emperor class, of which only two holders are known; the elven heir is said to hold one, and Adin is quietly keeping Ken's class hidden. From Crimson's viewpoint, she has stopped diving because a rising heart rate triggers a dangerous skill, and her eyes of wisdom picked out Ken at the entrance exam as someone who could help. The five grandparents, a high-level party, ambush her; she ends the fight with a blade at one throat and says she wants to train Ken and perhaps bring him into her family. The grandmothers then question Ken's partners. The grandparents reveal that the family has been hired assassins for generations and let the work lapse after Ken's mother died, since she wanted him to be an adventurer. They are wealthy, own a private dungeon entrance, and describe a rival family holding entrances behind corporate fronts. They will stay near Halen, block outside threats, and leave the priestess to Ken. That night they carry him across the city on wind magic, and during a blackout Ken kills everyone in the convict guild's house. He asks them to restore the family. Dez, Charlotte and Fayeth vow to stand by him, and Ken and Fayeth spend their first night together, a soul bond elves treat as close to marriage. Adin and the grandparents welcome the match, and Ken sets his sights on the priestess's flag.

So far this book: Crimson drills the class on the boss's three phases. Ken arranges for Kendra and another party leader to photograph the priestess's camp once he has her flag, draining her points. News spreads that the convict guild was destroyed, including its jailed members, and Ken tells Harley he handled only the killings in the city. Crimson promises to expel the priestess the moment her points run out. At the dungeon entrance the priestess asks for a truce; Ken refuses and urges her party to abandon her. Meanwhile an elven royal censor, sent by a noble lady over the Emperor-class documents, confronts Adin; Crimson slices through her half-drawn sword, then follows her into the dungeon. Below, Dez watches the priestess's party through her summoned eye. Ken and Dez drive fribbits into its alarm wires until the guard removes them, and Ken knocks her out with chloroform and takes the flag. Kendra's group and Penelope's party agree to photograph the camp, but the priestess's party vanishes, seemingly returning to the surface each night. Dez tells Ken she would accept if he proposed. The party clears floor five and reaches level 5. Near the boss doors the censor appears with Crimson as her escort and offers to share details of Ken's class up to level 20. At the visitor center, Crimson states that the elven princess does not actually hold the Emperor class, and the censor admits the claim was staged by imperial order after the Naga halted the elven advance. Ken's class is the true one, tied to the first emperor. The censor asks him to share Absorb with the princess; he agrees only to visit the elven world. His level-5 skill is Discharge.

Through the end: Crimson reports that Marlow, guarding the school's image, let the priestess's Class B teacher grant her party off-schedule classes. A flag taken by force still counts, and the priestess has one point left. Crimson calls the censor harmless but warns Ken about the elven world, then sets a goal of floor 20 by the end of his second term; when Ken takes her hand, red static flares and she leaves abruptly. The party hunts the priestess on the third floor. She turns out to be a temple lord whose fire Ken absorbs or outruns, and she overpowers him on holy ground until Metamorphosis evens the fight. Dez chokes her from behind, her party surrenders, and Ken takes four flags and their loot, but the priestess stays below in the first safe zone. In the class trial, Ken's party beats the boggart boss in three phases and passes the semester. In the safe zone one of Ken's grandmothers collects the party. In Marlow's office the priestess's father threatens to cut Halen off from CIDs; Crimson destroys his tablet, bans the family from the grounds, and tells Marlow they will be dead by nightfall. Ken's grandfather boards the father's plane as its pilot, learns the guards bear the snake-and-arch mark of an organization he hates, kills the co-pilot and crashes over empty forest. The grandmothers fight the guards, and the grandfather kills a wave of portal-summoned reinforcements. The father kills Ken with a shield blast, and a grandmother revives him. Crimson arrives, saying she came to congratulate Ken, and turns the father to dust with her red static. The tattooed portal caster escapes, and Fayeth kills the priestess, finding no comfort in it. Ken and Fayeth face four years of leveling ahead, with training under the grandparents to come.
